post.description:
Retrieve ontology classes, value sets, and values based on CEDAR value constraints. This endpoint takes a controlled term field specification and any user-supplied initial characters and returns conforming values.

Some sample calls in Insomnia (https://insomnia.rest/) format are available at https://github.com/metadatacenter/cedar-util/blob/master/api-calls/CEDAR_Insomnia_API_calls.json.

Note that in some cases, the server will need to sort the results obtained from BioPortal and the original pagination information will not be valid any more. In those situations, the values of some of the pagination fields returned as part of the results (e.g., pageCount, nextPage, etc.) cannot be computed consistently, and the server will assign a 'null' value to those fields.

requestBody.description: Object that encapsulates the information needed to run the search query. The "valueConstraints" field specification is based on CEDAR's "_valueConstraints" field. See https://more.metadatacenter.org/tools-training/outreach/cedar-template-model for more details.

200.description: A paginated list of search results

post.description: Search the local terminology store at a named version or the current one, across the constraint types a controlled-term field can carry: ontology, branch, class and valueSet. Returns per-type counts and each type's first page, and describes every source it searched — the version that answered, and whether a constraint on it can be pinned.

requestBody.description: The query, the constraint types to answer, and the sources to search. A source names the version to search it at, or none to search the current one. Keys are the versioned value-constraint specification's, so a result can become a constraint entry without translation.

200.description: Results, and the sources that produced them

400.description: A request the server will not answer

503.description: No local terminology store is configured

get.description: The chain of ancestors above a term, root first, and what hangs directly below it. A search result names a term; whether it is the right term is a question about its neighbourhood, and two concepts with one label are told apart by nothing else. With versionId, answered from that release's snapshot: a hierarchy belongs to a release, and a term's parent can move between two of them. Without it, from the cross-snapshot index, which holds each ontology's current version. Children are alphabetical and capped; offset asks for the next page of them.

404.description: No such release, a release without that term, or a term the index does not hold

503.description: No local terminology store is configured

get.summary: Where a term sits in its ontology
